# Guardana Control

> Guardana Control puts your rules between an AI agent and its tools. Each call that goes through it is allowed, blocked or held for a person before it runs.

This is alpha software and not a security boundary: do not deploy it as one. What exists today is listed on the status page, each capability with its label, implemented, experimental or planned: https://control.guardana.dev/docs/status

## Get started

- [Try the demo](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/get-started/try-the-demo): Start a plane in front of two vulnerable MCP servers, answer a held call, pause a server, read the trail and the counters, and run the demo's scenarios.

## Guides

- [Back up and restore a plane](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/back-up-and-restore-a-plane): Copy a stopped plane's floors, runs, pause file and stop list, and after a loss raise them back so no floor ends lower, every run is closed and no hold resumes.
- [Connect an existing MCP setup](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/connect-an-existing-mcp-setup): Put the plane between an MCP client and a server you already use, classify the server's tools, hold its writes for approval, and end in a local report.
- [Decide a tool of your own](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/decide-a-tool-of-your-own): Serve the enforcement API, classify your tools by name, and have a client ask before each call and report how it ended, under one policy and trail.
- [Keep two tasks apart](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/keep-two-tasks-apart): Open a run per task in a runs directory, point a plane at it, and give each agent its token, so what one task took in never decides another's calls.
- [Let a decision point veto calls](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/let-a-decision-point-veto): Point the gateway at an AuthZEN decision point, write the two rules that let it veto a scope, test what each answer does, and check the plane before it serves.
- [Read the evidence from a program](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/read-the-evidence-from-a-program): Export a trail file in the versioned format, resume where the last export stopped, and rebuild each call's lifecycle without importing the project's internals.
- [Run the gateway in a container](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/run-in-a-container): Run the release image of the gateway with Docker, with its evidence on a volume and its port reachable from the host alone.
- [Run the gateway](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/run-the-gateway): Set up a plane's policy files, start the MCP gateway in OBSERVE, keep its policy confirmed, read its health, classify the tools it sees, and move it to ENFORCE.
- [Supervise and stop a run](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/supervise-and-stop-a-run): Run the refund example by hand on a live plane, supervise the run against its procedure, read its page, and stop it on a confirmed finding.
- [Test a procedure](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/test-a-procedure): Lint a procedure document, then prove what supervise finds with cases that state a run, its evidence and every expected finding.
- [Watch a plane without a collector](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/watch-a-plane-without-a-collector): Run the collector the gateway binary ships, point a plane at it with its credential, read each request's trail in the segments it writes, and prune them.
- [Watch an egress proxy](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/watch-an-egress-proxy): Have Envoy or Squid write their access log as JSON lines, import it as observations, and see in the coverage map the destinations the proxy logged.
- [Write and test a policy](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/guides/write-and-test-a-policy): Write an agent-policy/v1alpha1 document, lint it, prove what it decides with cases, sign it into the bundle a plane loads, and vouch that the bundle is current.

## Concepts

- [Approvals and the held request](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/approvals-and-the-held-call): What the enforcement point holds when a call needs an approval, what a retry must equal to resume it, and the ways a hold ends.
- [Architecture](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/architecture): The system in context, its containers, the request path from a proposed action to a decision and its evidence, the dependency rule, and where it is going.
- [Control and supervision](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/control-and-supervision): The 1.0 goal for connected observation, procedure checks and scoped reactions, with today's alpha and the three API roles kept explicit.
- [Enforcement modes](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/enforcement-modes): What each mode does with the kernel's decision, what it needs from an adapter, and which modes this build runs.
- [Evidence and the spool](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/evidence-and-the-spool): The trail every call leaves, the order its events may take, and how the spool keeps them on disk before an exporter sees them.
- [Glossary](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/glossary): One name per concept, as the pages and the code use it, with the symbol or path that defines each.
- [How a call is decided](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/how-a-call-is-decided): From a proposed action to one of five verdicts and the action enforced for it, including what happens when the kernel cannot decide.
- [The MCP gateway](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/mcp-gateway): How a tools/call becomes a decision, an authorized set of bytes and a trail, before the server sees it.
- [Observations, coverage, supervision and a stop](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/observations-coverage-and-supervision): How what a source reports, the coverage map, the supervisor's findings and a stop of one run fit together, and what each promises and does not.
- [Privacy](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/privacy): What the plane records about a call, where each record goes and who can read it, how long it stays, and that nothing goes to the project.
- [Signed operations](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/signed-operations): What is signed in Guardana Control, by whom, what each signature proves, what is not signed, and what a signature never proves.
- [Threat model](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/concepts/threat-model): What the plane protects, from whom, what it does about each attacker today with the code and the test behind it, and where it stops.

## Reference

- [Benchmarks](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/benchmarks): What three calls on the authorization path and one tool call through the gateway cost on one machine, how they are measured, and what the numbers are not.
- [Claude Code hooks](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/claude-code-hooks): What the claude-code hook profile covers, the hook settings it needs, what the bridge reads and answers per event, and the gaps it leaves.
- [Command line](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/cli): The two binaries, what each prints as its help, and the exit statuses they share.
- [Configuration](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/configuration): Every key the gateway reads, with its environment variable, kind, default, whether it is required and the spellings it takes.
- [The approvals page](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/console): What guardana-control console serves, what it prints, what it refuses and what it cannot tell you.
- [Coverage](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/coverage): What guardana-control coverage reads, its inventory, the state of each declared path and each undeclared egress host, the join, and its exit status.
- [Dev mode](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/dev): What guardana-gateway dev lays out, refuses, prints and stops, and how --scenario runs each scenario on a plane of its own.
- [Egress access log](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/egress-access-log): The descriptor of an egress proxy's access log, how its lines map to connection observations, what is never read, each refusal, and the trust it claims.
- [Failure modes](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/failure-modes): What a plane does when its collector, spool, decision point, upstream, pause file, stop list, freshness statement or clock fails, or it is killed holding calls.
- [MCP enforcement coverage](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/mcp-coverage): Per revision, transport and method, what the gateway enforces today and what it does not.
- [Metrics](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/metrics): Every metric a plane answers on /metrics, with its type, its label, the statistic it reads and what it counts.
- [Obligations](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/obligations): The catalogue of obligation types a policy rule may name, the parameters each takes, and what the tree does with one.
- [Observations](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/observations): The source descriptor and its kinds, what an import of OpenTelemetry GenAI spans keeps and drops, the observation log and its export.
- [Policy explain](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/policy-explain): What `guardana-control policy explain` reads, every line it prints, which rule decided and which input a rule could not read, and its bounds.
- [Policy document format](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/policy-format): Every member of an agent-policy/v1alpha1 document, the values each admits, the bounds, and the members of a policy test case.
- [Signed reaction](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/reaction-signed): How a signed plane takes its route, stop list header and lifts from roster operators, holds them to a stop list floor, and which commands sign them.
- [Reaction](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/reaction): The signed route, the stop list and the commands that write them, and how a plane refuses a stopped run's calls and reports its stops.
- [Reason codes](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/reason-codes): Every reason code a decision may carry, with its number and the verdict it usually accompanies.
- [Run view](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/run-view): The page guardana-control supervise --view draws for one run, what each mark on it means, and what the command refuses to overwrite.
- [Runs](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/runs): The runs directory, what runs open, close, list and prune print and refuse, and what a plane with runs.dir does with a token.
- [Scenario format](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/scenario-format): Every member of an agent-scenario/v1alpha1 document, how scenario run holds a live plane to one, and what it exits with.
- [Starter policy packs](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/starter-packs): The read-only and approval-for-writes packs, what each decides, what it assumes about the plane, the cases that prove it, and what it leaves unguarded.
- [Supervision](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/supervision): The procedure document, what guardana-control supervise checks for one opened run, the finding record and its log, and how notify delivers findings.
- [Format versions](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/versions): Every versioned file and message a user writes or reads, the version this tree writes, the versions it reads, and how stable each is.
- [action_envelope.proto](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/wire/action_envelope): The messages and enums of action_envelope.proto as the compiled descriptor declares them, each field with its number, cardinality and type.
- [approval.proto](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/wire/approval): The messages and enums of approval.proto as the compiled descriptor declares them, each field with its number, cardinality and type.
- [bundle.proto](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/wire/bundle): The messages and enums of bundle.proto as the compiled descriptor declares them, each field with its number, cardinality and type.
- [common.proto](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/wire/common): The messages and enums of common.proto as the compiled descriptor declares them, each field with its number, cardinality and type.
- [decision.proto](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/wire/decision): The messages and enums of decision.proto as the compiled descriptor declares them, each field with its number, cardinality and type.
- [event.proto](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/wire/event): The messages and enums of event.proto as the compiled descriptor declares them, each field with its number, cardinality and type.
- [finding.proto](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/wire/finding): The messages and enums of finding.proto as the compiled descriptor declares them, each field with its number, cardinality and type.
- [result.proto](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/reference/wire/result): The messages and enums of result.proto as the compiled descriptor declares them, each field with its number, cardinality and type.

## Specification

- [Wire contracts](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/contracts): What the v1 messages are versioned by, what a receiver refuses them for, and how the evidence events chain.

## Extending

- [Writing an adapter](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/extending/adapters): The internal seam a protocol adapter implements, the capabilities it declares, and the conformance each one owes.
- [Adding a coding runtime's hooks](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/extending/runtime-profiles): The profile a coding runtime's hook protocol is described by, what the hook bridge does with it, and what a profile needs before its page may claim anything.

## Project

- [Adoption and incident workflows](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/adoption-and-incident-workflows): Planned acceptance requirements for MCP setup, coding hooks, tool-definition review, policy simulation and incident review.
- [Delivery backlog](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/backlog): Planned work ordered by user value, with dependencies and observable acceptance checks.
- [Changelog](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/changelog): What each release changed, and what is unreleased on main.
- [Dependencies](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/dependencies): Every direct dependency and pinned tool of the module, why the standard library will not do, its licence and whether it sits in the request path.
- [Roadmap](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/roadmap): What has to become true, in the order it is planned.
- [Implementation status](https://control.guardana.dev/docs/status): What exists in this repository today, component by component, the one inventory every other page points to.
